pages.x: The Taliban, a movement of religious students that had taken Kabul in 1996, ruled most of Afghanistan by their strict reading of Islamic law. Girls were barred from school, music and television were banned, and thieves had their hands cut off. They gave a home to Osama bin Laden, and after 11 September they refused to hand him over.

From 7 October 2001 American and British planes bombed the Taliban, while a few hundred American special forces, some of them on horseback, rode with the Afghan fighters of the Northern Alliance. Kabul fell on 13 November, and Kandahar in December. Bin Laden slipped away from the caves of Tora Bora into Pakistan.

Hamid Karzai became the head of a new government, and in 2004 he was elected president. Girls went back to school, millions of refugees came home, and women sat in parliament. But the new state was riddled with corruption, and the NATO troops sent to keep the peace, from about fifty countries, were spread thin.

From 2006 the Taliban came back, from safe havens across the border in Pakistan, with roadside bombs and suicide attacks. In 2009 President Barack Obama sent 30,000 more soldiers, bringing American forces to about 100,000, but the Taliban could not be beaten. In 2011 bin Laden was found and killed in Pakistan.

About 2,400 American soldiers died, and over 1,100 from allied countries, 457 of them British. Some 69,000 Afghan soldiers and police were killed, and over 50,000 Taliban and other fighters. Most painful of all, more than 46,000 Afghan civilians died in air strikes, bombings and crossfire.

In February 2020 the United States signed a deal with the Taliban in Doha, in Qatar, promising to withdraw all its troops. The Afghan government was left out of the talks. President Joe Biden kept to it, and in May 2021 the last soldiers began to leave.

As the troops left, the Afghan army collapsed. On 15 August 2021 President Ashraf Ghani fled, and the Taliban walked into Kabul. Thousands of desperate Afghans crowded the airport, and some clung to the side of an American plane as it took off. A suicide bomber killed over 180 people at the gates. On 30 August the last American soldier left.

America's longest war ended where it began, with the Taliban in power. They have again shut girls out of school after the age of twelve and banned women from most work, making Afghanistan the only country in the world where girls cannot go to secondary school.
pts: The Taliban took Kabul again in 2021
